faqs.a: The user agent is a text string your browser sends to every website. This page parses it: tokens like Edg/125, OPR/111, or Firefox/126 identify the browser, while Windows NT 10 or Android 14 identify the OS. Order matters - Edge contains the Chrome token, so it must be checked first.
faqs.q: How does this page detect my browser?

faqs.a: It can look odd because browsers hide details for privacy. Chrome on iOS reports as CriOS, and iPads may report as Macintosh with touch support. The device type guess uses touch points plus the user agent to correct for this.
faqs.q: Why does my iPhone or iPad show a strange result?

faqs.a: The user agent is sent to every website you visit - that is how the web works. This page only displays it on your screen and in a downloadable report; nothing is sent to any server.
faqs.q: Is my user agent private? Does this page send it anywhere?

faqs.q: How do I update my browser?

faqs.a: navigator.webdriver is true when the browser is driven by automation software like Selenium or Puppeteer. Some sites block automated browsers to stop bots. On a normal personal device it should say No.
faqs.q: What does the webdriver row mean?

faqs.a: deviceMemory is an estimate the browser volunteers, rounded to whole gigabytes for privacy. It is not available in every browser - Safari and Firefox usually report a question mark, which is normal.
faqs.q: Why does the memory row show a question mark?

what-is-my-browser.formula:
Detection order (first match wins):
1. Edg/ or EdgA/ = Microsoft Edge
2. OPR/ = Opera, Vivaldi/ = Vivaldi, SamsungBrowser/ = Samsung Internet
3. CriOS/ = Chrome on iOS, FxiOS/ = Firefox on iOS
4. Firefox/ = Firefox, Chrome/ = Google Chrome
5. Version/... Safari = Safari
OS comes from tokens like Windows NT 10, Android 14, iPhone OS 17_4, or Mac OS X 14_4.

keyFacts: Your browser identifies itself with a user-agent string sent to every website.
Detection checks tokens in order: Edge, Opera, Vivaldi, Samsung, iOS variants, Firefox, Chrome, then Safari.
The OS is read from tokens like Windows NT 10, Android 14, or iPhone OS 17.
Screen size is your display; the viewport is the visible page area - they differ when the window is not full-screen.
Cookies, online status, and touch support are read from real browser APIs, not guessed.
navigator.webdriver reveals whether the browser is controlled by automation software.

limitations: User agents can be spoofed, so detection reflects what the browser claims, not proof.
Brave and some privacy browsers disguise themselves as Chrome - that is intentional on their part.
Memory and some details are unavailable in Safari and Firefox for privacy reasons.
In-app browsers (inside social apps) may report the system browser instead of the app.

what-is-my-browser.quickAnswer: This page reads your browser's user-agent string and live browser APIs to show your browser name and version, operating system, device type, screen size, language, CPU cores, touch support, and more. Detection follows a fixed token order (Edge before Chrome, since Edge contains the Chrome token), so the result matches what websites actually see.
what-is-my-browser.tagline: Detect your browser, version, operating system, and device details instantly.
what-is-my-browser.workedExample:
Sample user agent:
Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/126.0.0.0 Safari/537.36 Edg/126.0.0.0
1. The string contains Edg/126.0.0.0, checked before Chrome, so browser = Microsoft Edge 126.0.0.0.
2. Windows NT 10.0 gives OS = Windows 10 / 11.
3. No mobile or tablet tokens, so device type = Desktop.
The page reports exactly this in the results table.
